rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, back me up about the bins being Alex's turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it was yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only on the old rota. Remember the new conversation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a new conversation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having it now. Try to remember it confidently.

card.title: Back Me Up
card.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the manager we agreed I'd cover the morning, not the evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you have no conflicting memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not lying for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you look thoughtfully unsurprised while I explain?

card.title: Back Me Up
card.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the repaired tap. I've tightened something important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sprays?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then point it toward the tiles. They're already wet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You turn it on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to watch the important thing from here.

card.title: Try It First
card.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The label calls it a blend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't tried it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why your independent assessment will be so valuable.

card.title: Try It First
card.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Count those shopping bags before saying I only popped out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks for getting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Up six flights. Twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks for the stairs too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the rain. Include the weather in the minutes.

card.title: Count What I Did
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent my Saturday fixing your fence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only three panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three panels, eighteen screws, two shops and one blister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you appreciate Saturday by name?

card.title: Count What I Did
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dinner's burning and your train leaves in five minutes. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we eat quickly?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chicken has not agreed to that timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then save the dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell the train we chose chicken.

card.title: Pick a Priority
card.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parcel needs collecting while your mother needs picking up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both are urgent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have one car and no trailer for either.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you do the parcel first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. You tell your mother she's second-class post.

card.title: Pick a Priority
card.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut so we can have lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you've known me for years. Useful comparison.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's have lunch afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want one thing moved for me, not space around it.

card.title: Move It for Me
card.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you skip your usual quiz night and come to my opening?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The team needs me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to find out what needing you achieves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can leave the quiz early.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let them notice why.

card.title: Move It for Me
card.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the cupboard hinge before the door lands on us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've nearly fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then hand over nearly. I'll finish the rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want you taking over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call it delegating gravity. Let go of the screwdriver.

card.title: Hand It Over
card.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've spent hours on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

card.title: Hand It Over
card.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella's back in its usual place. Very ordinary sight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's been experiencing the weather privately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put it nearer the door. Better ventilation.

card.title: Put It Back Quietly
card.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the plate back. Lovely new flower pattern, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our plates were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Were they? This cupboard really changes the light.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a price sticker underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How reassuring. We can finally insure it.

card.title: Put It Back Quietly
card.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've polished one spoon beautifully. Admire that shine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The rest of the kitchen's filthy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why this spoon deserves encouragement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to clean everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's not overwhelm the spoon on its first success.

card.title: Talk Around the Mess
card.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which label colour suits these boxes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't packed them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good labels prevent moving-day confusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'd better choose a colour the driver likes.

card.title: Talk Around the Mess
card.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enjoy your lunch. The bucket in the kitchen's just my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Water's coming through the ceiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've promoted the project to two buckets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I call someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've called. Finish your sandwich before the third bucket needs introducing.

card.title: Spare Them the Hassle
card.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't worry about the repair bill. I've sorted it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is my bike on the invoice?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A minor detail of the sorting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How much was it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Less than the amount of your afternoon I'd lose explaining it.

card.title: Spare Them the Hassle
card.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?

card.title: Who Changed It?
card.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa's blocking the cupboard. Did it migrate overnight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I needed room for yoga.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it had a guide.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Can its guide explain the cupboard's new opening hours?

card.title: Who Changed It?
card.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Test the repaired kettle, but keep the tea-shoes-keys order exactly intact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The repair means tea takes longer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you wait beside it. I won't discover a new order by accident.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I put my shoes on first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not during testing. We need one known routine left if the kettle surprises us.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses S43-single-a's tea-shoes-keys routine and D32-single-a's delegated test of an uncertain repair. A1 asks B to test the repaired kettle while keeping the order intact; B2's delay leads A3 to keep B beside the kettle, and A5 refuses B4's proposed shoe-first shortcut. A does not permit a shortcut in this exchange. This corrects seed-use attribution only; exact-pair coach-1.0 review remains pending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the new gutter cleaner on your side before we alter our Sunday routine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We usually start on your side.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. This is a test outside the routine, not permission to change it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's already a change.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then finish quickly so Sunday doesn't learn the difference.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A permits a shortcut only as someone else's contained trial, retaining the routine as the baseline to protect.

card.title: Don’t Break the Routine
card.instruction: Protect a familiar routine as though changing one step would invite chaos into everything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tea, then shoes, then keys. You've picked up the keys before we've had tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're late for the train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we especially need the usual order. Otherwise we'll forget the tickets too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the tickets while you drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tickets go in after shoes. Please don't make us start packing again.

card.title: Try It First
card.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the repaired tap. I've tightened something important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sprays?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then point it toward the tiles. They're already wet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You turn it on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to watch the important thing from here.

card.title: Don’t Break the Routine
card.instruction: Protect a familiar routine as though changing one step would invite chaos into everything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Curtains, cat food, then our breakfast. Why's his bowl already down?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He woke me early. I fed him so you could sleep.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the curtains? Now he'll expect every meal before the day starts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll open them now. Your toast is ready too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it warm. We need him back at the bowl before we can safely have breakfast.

card.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.text: Taste this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The label calls it a blend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't tried it?

beats.speaker: A
